questions.prompt: Explain the bug ADR-0015 fixes: what did "mastered" promise, why was the promise false at the baseline, and why was that the normal path rather than an edge case?

keyPoints.text: Mastery is defined as two reps, and the README promises two spaced correct answers.
keyPoints.quote: ADR-0009 defines mastery as two reps, and the README promises "two spaced correct answers".

keyPoints.text: The baseline scheduler never read dueAt, so two answers a minute apart mastered a card.
keyPoints.quote: so two correct answers a minute apart mastered a card (F-01)

keyPoints.text: Sessions re-serve non-due cards on purpose, so this was the ordinary path.
keyPoints.quote: Sessions deliberately re-serve non-due cards (module drills, "Another round"), so this was the normal path.

keyPoints.text: The self-test asserted the bug as a pass.
keyPoints.quote: `check.js` asserted the bug as a pass.

keyPoints.text: Learners study at roughly, not exactly, the same time each day, which shapes the fix.
keyPoints.quote: Learners study at roughly, but not exactly, the same time each day.

questions.prompt: State the decision precisely: what does a correct answer before the due date change and not change, when is a card due, and what happens to wrong answers and due dates?

keyPoints.text: An early correct answer is practice.
keyPoints.quote: We treat a correct answer given before the card is due as **practice**.

keyPoints.text: Practice advances the counters but leaves the schedule untouched.
keyPoints.quote: It advances `attempts`, `correct` and `lastAnsweredAt`, and leaves `reps`, `ease`, `intervalDays` and `dueAt` unchanged.

keyPoints.text: A card is due if never answered or once now reaches dueAt.
keyPoints.quote: A card is due if it has never been answered, or if `now >= dueAt`.

keyPoints.text: A wrong answer is always a lapse or failure, back in 10 minutes.
keyPoints.quote: A wrong answer is a lapse (`reps > 0`) or a failure (`reps === 0`) at any time, due again in 10 minutes.

keyPoints.text: Day-scale due dates snap to local start of day, so back in 1 day means any time tomorrow.
keyPoints.quote: so "back in 1 day" means any time tomorrow

keyPoints.text: Intervals are capped at 180 days and practice earns 1 XP.
keyPoints.quote: Intervals are capped at 180 days.

keyPoints.text: schedule returns an outcome that the answer response carries.
keyPoints.quote: and the answer response carries it. Practice earns 1 XP.

questions.prompt: Weigh the trade-offs: what does the decision buy and cost, which alternatives were rejected and why, and where does it break first?

keyPoints.text: It buys honest progress: mastery, unlocks and levels now mean what the README says, and a replayed POST can no longer move the schedule.
keyPoints.quote: a replayed POST can no longer move the schedule

keyPoints.text: Cost: learners who farmed repeats before the change see their XP drop once, at upgrade.
keyPoints.quote: learners who farmed repeats before this change see their XP drop once, at upgrade

keyPoints.text: Cost: extra practice in a module drill moves nothing on the schedule, so the client has to tell the learner via outcome and reason.
keyPoints.quote: extra practice in a module drill moves nothing, and the client must say so

keyPoints.text: It constrains future work: any new session mode must tag the non-due cards it serves as practice.
keyPoints.quote: any new session mode must tag non-due cards `practice`

keyPoints.text: A minimum gap since the last answer was turned down: it would add a new timing constant beside the schedule, while keying on dueAt reuses the schedule each card already has.
keyPoints.quote: A minimum gap since the last answer.

keyPoints.text: Never serving non-due cards was also turned down: it changes what sessions hand out, but the guard has to sit in schedule(), the one place every answer passes through.
keyPoints.quote: Never serve non-due cards.

keyPoints.text: Due-to-the-millisecond was rejected because earlier study would count as practice.
keyPoints.quote: It turns "back in 1 day" into practice for anyone who studies earlier than yesterday.

keyPoints.text: It breaks first with learners in several time zones on one server.
keyPoints.quote: Learners in several time zones on one server. "Local start of day" is the server's zone.
